title: Stability and dynamics of extradenticle modulates its function.
authors: Singh, Aakanksha; Acharya, Bidisha; Mukherjee, Beas; Boorla, Veda Sheersh; Boral, Soumendu; Maiti, Snigdha; De, Soumya
one_liner_zh: 该文通过NMR和MD模拟研究HOX辅因子EXD的DNA结合螺旋中甘氨酸突变对蛋白稳定性与DNA结合亲和力的影响，聚焦TF-DNA互作机制，方法上采用MD/MMGBSA，高度匹配课题。
abstract: Extradenticle (EXD) is a partner protein of the HOX transcription factors and plays an important role in the development of Drosophila. It confers increased affinity and specificity of DNA-binding to the HOX proteins. However, the DNA-binding homeodomain of EXD has a significantly weaker affinity to DNA compared to the HOX homeodomains. Here, we show that a glycine residue (G290) in the middle of the EXD DNA-binding helix primarily results in this weaker binding. Glycine destabilizes helices. To probe its role in the stability and function of the protein, G290 was mutated to alanine. The intrinsic stability of the DNA-binding helix increased in the G290A mutant as observed by NMR studies and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. Also, NMR dynamics and MD simulation show that dynamic motions present in the wild-type protein are quenched in the mutant. This in turn resulted in increased stability of the entire homeodomain (DeltaDeltaG(G-->A) of -2.6 kcal/mol). Increased protein stability resulted in three-fold better DNA-binding affinity of the mutant as compared to the wild-type protein. Molecular mechanics with generalized Born and surface area solvation (MMGBSA) analysis of our MD simulation on DNA-bound models of both wild-type and mutant proteins shows that the contribution to binding is enhanced for most of the interface residues in the mutant compared to the wild-type. Interestingly, the flexible N-terminal arm makes more stable contact with the DNA minor groove in the mutant. We found that the two interaction sites i.e. the DNA-binding helix and the unstructured N-terminal arm influence each other via the bound DNA. These results provide an interesting conundrum: alanine at position 290 enhances both the stability and the DNA-binding affinity of the protein, however, evolution prefers glycine at this position. We have provided several plausible explanations for this apparent conundrum. The function of the EXD as a HOX co-factor requires its ability to discriminate similar DNA sequences, which is most likely comprom.
abstract_zh: Extradenticle (EXD) 是HOX转录因子的伴侣蛋白，在果蝇发育中发挥重要作用。它赋予HOX蛋白更高的DNA结合亲和力和特异性。然而，与HOX同源结构域相比，EXD的DNA结合同源结构域对DNA的亲和力显著较弱。在此，我们表明EXD DNA结合螺旋中部的甘氨酸残基（G290）主要导致这种较弱的结合。甘氨酸使螺旋不稳定。为了探究其在蛋白质稳定性和功能中的作用，将G290突变为丙氨酸。通过NMR研究和分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟观察到，G290A突变体中DNA结合螺旋的固有稳定性增加。此外，NMR动力学和分子动力学模拟显示，野生型蛋白质中存在的动态运动在突变体中被抑制。这进而导致整个同源结构域的稳定性增加（DeltaDeltaG(G-->A)为-2.6 kcal/mol）。蛋白质稳定性的增加使突变体的DNA结合亲和力比野生型蛋白质高三倍。我们对野生型和突变体蛋白质的DNA结合模型进行的分子力学广义Born和表面积溶剂化（MMGBSA）分析表明，与野生型相比，突变体中大多数界面残基对结合的贡献增强。有趣的是，在突变体中，柔性的N端臂与DNA小沟形成更稳定的接触。我们发现，两个相互作用位点，即DNA结合螺旋和非结构化N端臂，通过结合的DNA相互影响。这些结果提出了一个有趣的难题：第290位的丙氨酸增强了蛋白质的稳定性和DNA结合亲和力，然而，进化却偏好此位置的甘氨酸。我们为这一明显难题提供了几种合理的解释。EXD作为HOX辅因子的功能要求其能够区分相似的DNA序列，这很可能受到损害。
